/-- A set is a collection of elements of some type `α`.

relied on. Instead, `setOf` and membership of a set (`∈`) should be used to convert between sets
and predicates.

theorem Cantor : ∀ f : α → Set α, ¬Surjective f := by
  /-
    α : Type u_3
    ⊢ ∀ (f : α → Set α), Not (Function.Surjective f)
  -/
  intro f surjf
  /-
    α : Type u_3
    f : α → Set α
    surjf : Function.Surjective f
    ⊢ False
  -/
  let S := { i | i ∉ f i }
  /-
    α : Type u_3
    f : α → Set α
    surjf : Function.Surjective f
    S : Set α := setOf fun i => Not (Membership.mem (f i) i)
    ⊢ False
  -/
  rcases surjf S with ⟨j, h⟩
  have h₁ : j ∉ f j := by
    intro h'
    have : j ∉ f j := by rwa [h] at h'
    contradiction
  /-
    case intro
    α : Type u_3
    f : α → Set α
    surjf : Function.Surjective f
    S : Set α := setOf fun i => Not (Membership.mem (f i) i)
    j : α
    h : Eq (f j) S
    h₁ : Not (Membership.mem (f j) j)
    ⊢ False

  have h₂ : j ∈ S := h₁

    case intro
    α : Type u_3
    f : α → Set α
    surjf : Function.Surjective f
    S : Set α := setOf fun i => Not (Membership.mem (f i) i)
    j : α
    h : Eq (f j) S
    h₁ : Not (Membership.mem (f j) j)
    h₂ : Membership.mem S j

  -/

    case intro
    α : Type u_3
    f : α → Set α
    surjf : Function.Surjective f
    S : Set α := setOf fun i => Not (Membership.mem (f i) i)
    j : α

same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.
